summary: Mount Hood NF site on North Pinhead Butte, Wasco County: a cabin dated to the 1920s, a 1928 plan to occupy it in high fire-hazard periods, gone by 1945.

facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com both say the cabin was gone by 1945

staffing.status: planned occupancy only during periods of high fire hazard, per a January 1928 letter

events.note: Register and firelookout.com give only 'the 1920s' for the cabin; 1920 is a placeholder for the decade
Telephone line and trail built to the top of North Pinhead 'last year' per the January 10, 1928 letter
Forest plan to occupy these points only during periods of high fire hazard (letter dated January 10, 1928)
Cabin gone by 1945 per the register and firelookout.com; no source gives the cause
Registered August 26, 2010, nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: cabin built on this site in the 1920s and gone by 1945
evidence.quote: A cabin was built on this site in the 1920s and was gone by 1945.

evidence.supports: site is in the Mt. Hood National Forest
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
letter from a forest ranger at Wapinita to the Warm Springs forest supervisor
evidence.quote: Letter from Forest Ranger, Wapinita to Forest Supervisor, Warm Springs

evidence.supports: telephone line built to the top of North Pinhead the year before
evidence.quote: We constructed a telephone line to the top of north Pinhead last year

evidence.supports: trails built to the top of both points the year before
evidence.quote: Trails were constructed to the top of both these points last year

evidence.supports: intention to occupy these points only during periods of high fire hazard
evidence.quote: It is the intention to occupy these points during periods of high fire hazard only.

notes_for_editor: No source describes what remains on the site today, and none gives access. The cabin date is only 'the 1920s' in both sources; the 1920 event year is a decade placeholder. The 1928 letter describes a plan to occupy the points, not a record of anyone staying there. Source 3 is a transcription on a hobby site; the original Forest Service letter was not checked. The brief's record (gone, USFS, FFLOS 2010) is consistent with the sources, so no corrections.
